title: PER_NAME vs PER_ROLE: unique authorial names
rule: A unique authorial name created for a specific character is labeled PER_NAME, even if etymologically linked to a role or characteristic. Tests: sole identifier of the character; declines as a proper noun; used as a form of address; not replaceable by a generalized description without loss of meaning.
example_ru: «Обнимашка» ('little hugger'); «Марабу» ('Marabou'): A → PER_ROLE, B → PER_NAME
notes: Transferred into the NER guidelines as Rule 8.

title: PER_NAME vs PER_ROLE: anthropomorphic objects with a nickname
rule: PER_NAME if the word is used only as an address/reference to a specific, one-of-a-kind character; PER_ROLE if it remains a category/species description, even applied to a single character. Test: can you say 'one of the [X]'?
example_ru: «Жёлтый» ('Yellow', a flower character) vs «Одуванчики» ('Dandelions', a group)
notes: No occurrences in the released adjudication log: resolved during handbook compilation.

title: PER_NAME vs PER_ROLE: animal characters
rule: Animals acting as specific characters with individual traits and a unique name are PER_NAME; animals as a generic species or background role are PER_ROLE.
example_ru: «Марабу» (a named teacher) vs «Сова», «Снегирь», «Попугай» (species, no unique name)

title: PER_NAME vs PER_FAMILY: kinship roles as names
rule: PER_FAMILY for standard kinship words in the context of a specific family; PER_NAME when the kinship role becomes the character's unique authorial name. Test: can the word be used as a form of address independently of the kinship fact?
example_ru: «мама» vs «Обнимама», «Мама-паровоз», «Мама-Тигрица», «Папа-Тигр»
notes: The address test added to the NER guidelines as Rule 10.

title: Compound nouns with a kinship term: name vs. episodic metaphor
rule: A compound 'kinship word + noun' is PER_NAME only if it is a fixed authorial name used as the character's main identifier and form of address throughout the book; a one-off metaphorical comparison within an episode is PER_ROLE (one span over the whole compound).
example_ru: «мама-паровоз» as an episodic metaphor vs «Мама-паровоз» as a character's name in RUS-O_long_01
resolution: Episodic metaphor → PER_ROLE (one span); fixed authorial name → PER_NAME
notes: Clarification to A-1/A-4/A-7; appears untitled in the working handbook; assigned the identifier A-4a for machine readability; does not occur as a standalone precedent_id in the adjudication log.

title: PER_ROLE vs PER_FAMILY: collective kinship terms
rule: PER_FAMILY if the word denotes a kinship role relative to a specific child character (possessive anchoring or single-family context); PER_ROLE if used generically without a link to a specific family.
example_ru: «Дети бежали к морю» vs «Его родители работали в саду»
notes: Status raised to STABLE: the possessive-anchoring criterion confirmed without contradiction on all discovered cases.

title: Spans of compound names: splitting into parts
rule: A fixed phrase forming a character's single name (name + neologistic patronymic/surname; fixed recognizable names) is annotated as ONE span labeled PER_NAME, regardless of the number of words.
example_ru: «Дед Мороз»: A → one span PER_ROLE; B → two spans «Дед»+«Мороз», both PER_NAME. «Керосин Бензинович» (8 mentions): A → one span PER_NAME; B → two spans each time
resolution: One span over the full name, PER_NAME
notes: ✎ Corrected from data: the real pattern is 'one span vs. two spans', not 'longer vs. shorter span'. A separate technical defect found: one duplicated span with two labels at identical offsets - an interface glitch, to be fixed in the data.

title: Spans of compound object designations: splitting into parts
rule: An object designation consisting of an attributive adjective and the role-bearing noun is annotated as ONE span over the whole phrase, labeled PER_ROLE; annotating the adjective alone is incomplete annotation.
example_ru: «СНЕГОУБОРОЧНАЯ МАШИНА»: A → one span over both words, PER_ROLE; B → span over the adjective only
resolution: One span over the whole phrase, PER_ROLE

title: Missed entities: single-word spans without a head noun
rule: Not yet decided. Two subtypes identified among the 360 preliminarily found single-word spans: (i) an adjective without its head noun - probable technical artifact, proposed not to count as a separate entity; (ii) «природа» ('nature') in a personifying context - a substantive open question about the limits of anthropomorphization.
example_ru: «маленький» separately from «слонёнок»; «мудрой природе»
resolution: Pending: both subtypes must be resolved on the full 360-case sample before the next annotation round
notes: The aggregate figure (360) is uninformative without the subtype breakdown; use with caution.

title: PER_ROLE: social relations outside the family
rule: Words denoting stable social relations («друзья», «приятели», «товарищи») are PER_ROLE when referring to specific characters within the world of the book rather than used abstractly.
example_ru: «— Эй, а где все твои друзья?»

title: Non-entities: verbs, prepositions, function words
rule: Only noun phrases denoting entities are annotated. Not entities: verbs; prepositions and conjunctions; adjectives not forming an independent noun phrase (except substantivized ones); nouns denoting attributes/patterns/materials; verse elements (rhymes, onomatopoeia, interjections); adverbs.
example_ru: «засыпает»; «в горошек»; «огромная»; «Бак» (rhyme)

title: Social and professional roles
rule: Words and phrases denoting social, professional, or functional roles are PER_ROLE if they denote a function/profession/status, are not a unique authorial name, and are not a kinship term of a specific family. Compound roles are annotated as one span.
example_ru: «сыщик», «воспитатель», «белый клоун», «воздушные гимнасты»

title: PER_ROLE: vehicle and object categories without unique names
rule: Words denoting categories of vehicles or objects that appear without a unique name are annotated as PER_ROLE when they act as characters or salient objects in the narrative.
example_ru: «вертолёты» 'helicopters' (RUS-T_medium_02): missed by annotator B, annotated PER_ROLE by A
notes: New precedent formulated during the second half of adjudication (books processed after the initial 13-book subset); extends the A-11 role family to inanimate vehicle categories.

title: Segmentation: direct-speech utterance + speech verb
rule: A direct-speech utterance and the immediately following speech verb with an intonational characteristic are annotated as ONE sentiment unit if the speech verb carries no emotional information distinct from the utterance.
example_ru: «— Обними меня, мама! — просил он перед сном.»: A → two units; B → one unit
resolution: One unit, labeled by the resulting emotion
notes: The most frequent segmentation-disagreement pattern (500+ multi-span groups of ~3,360 matched pairs). Transferred into the sentiment guidelines as Rule 8.

title: Exclamation with an explicit joy marker → positive
rule: Exclamatory sentences with explicit markers of joy/delight («О!», «Ура!», «Как красиво!») are +1 POSITIVE; without an explicit marker → 0 NEUTRAL.
example_ru: «О, это был самый настоящий цветущий сад!»: A → +1, B → 0
notes: Requires verification on exclamations with other markers («Какой ужас!», «Вот это да!»).

title: Fear-as-metaphor resolved by care within the same sentence
rule: If a phrase mentions worries/fear but the same sentence expresses care/support, the label follows the resulting emotion (care), not the trigger word.
example_ru: «— Мне бы хотелось спрятать тебя от всех тревог на свете.»: A → -1, B → +1
notes: Contrast with B-4: direction of emotion (care for another vs. own remorse) and presence of resolution within the sentence.

title: Remorse without immediate resolution → negative
rule: If a character expresses remorse and no immediate positive resolution follows in the same/next sentence, the label remains -1 NEGATIVE.
example_ru: «— Значит, я зря обидел бегемотика... И обезьянку.»: A → -1, B → 0

title: Question without explicit emotion markers → neutral
rule: Questions without explicit anxiety/fear markers are 0 NEUTRAL unless an explicitly negative emotion follows from the formulation or context.
notes: Thin boundary with Rule 1 cases («Куда делся малыш?» → -1): decided by a loss-implying formulation or a broader anxiety context.

title: Idyllic description of the world
rule: Landscape/expository descriptions receive +1 POSITIVE if they contain explicit positive evaluative features (warmth, care, beauty, coziness, abundance) rather than merely stating facts.
example_ru: «В одной тёплой стране, где солнце заботливо согревало землю...»

title: Request for closeness
rule: Utterances expressing a need for love, support, or physical closeness are +1 POSITIVE when the emotional focus is on attachment and care.
example_ru: «— Обними меня, мама! — просил он перед сном.»
notes: Consistent with the B-3 principle: the resulting emotion is set by the overall emotional direction.

title: Condescending or mentoring intonation without conflict
rule: Speech verbs and remarks conveying condescension, confidence, or a mentor's stance are not labeled negative in the absence of conflict, mockery, humiliation, or suffering.
example_ru: «— Разумеется, — хмыкнул Марабу, посмотрев на неё сверху вниз.»

title: Positive imagery in the context of a looming threat
rule: Traditionally positive natural imagery does not receive +1 if the immediate context shows it becoming part of an unfavorable situation; if the negative is not yet expressed in the fragment but the positive reading is cancelled by neighbors, choose 0 NEUTRAL.
example_ru: «Солнце всё так же лениво выкатывалось на небосклон и дарило миру своё тепло.»

title: Care under adverse circumstances
rule: Actions aimed at helping, caring, or supporting others receive +1 POSITIVE even against an unfavorable background; the act of care determines the resulting emotion.
example_ru: «Каждое утро Обнимашка ... поливал цветы, поникшие от жары.»

title: Unfinished objection
rule: Unfinished utterances expressing doubt or an attempted objection are neutral if the negative emotion/conflict appears only in the following utterance.
example_ru: «— Но...»; «А если...»; «Подожди...»

title: A character's favorite activity or place
rule: Utterances describing a favorite activity, habit, or place are +1 POSITIVE if they express pleasure, attachment, comfort, or calm; a later unfavorable event does not change this fragment's label. Markers: любил, нравилось, обожал, с удовольствием.
example_ru: «Он очень любил сидеть рядом с водой и смотреть на своё отражение.»

title: A character's helpless reaction
rule: Brief replies, gestures of helplessness, or withdrawal are -1 NEGATIVE if they express loneliness, loss, powerlessness, or consequences of misfortune.
example_ru: «— Ква. — Лягушка развела лапками и прыгнула в кусты.»

title: Statement of loss or destruction
rule: Utterances stating the loss, destruction, or serious deterioration of a significant object are -1 NEGATIVE; the focus on damage/loss determines the label. Markers: то, что осталось; всё погибло; он уже не тот.
example_ru: «— Точнее, то, что от него осталось.»

title: Value and the wish to preserve the beautiful
rule: Utterances expressing admiration of beauty or a wish to preserve it are +1 POSITIVE; an unfavorable context does not cancel their positive orientation.
example_ru: «— Чтобы мы могли им любоваться!..»

title: Acknowledgment of good intentions
rule: Utterances acknowledging another's good intentions with understanding instead of condemnation are +1 POSITIVE even in a difficult situation.
example_ru: «— Ты хотел как лучше, — покачала головой Обнимама.»

title: Verbalization of a negative emotion
rule: Utterances directly naming a character's negative emotions («боялся», «грустил», «испугался») are -1 NEGATIVE regardless of the speaker or a supportive context.
example_ru: «— А ещё ты очень боялся.»

title: Fixation on the source of misfortune
rule: If a character concentrates solely on the object of loss or threat out of fear/anxiety/sadness, the fragment is -1 NEGATIVE.
example_ru: «Поэтому смотрел лишь в высыхающий пруд.»

title: Reframing the situation through support
rule: Questions/utterances aimed at broadening perspective, overcoming fear, or finding hope are +1 POSITIVE even if formally interrogative.
example_ru: «Но что ты увидишь, если поднимешь голову?»

title: Incomprehension or clarification
rule: Questions/utterances of incomprehension or clarification are 0 NEUTRAL in the absence of a negative emotional reaction.
example_ru: «— Что — большая река? — не понял Марабу.»

title: Pointing out a limitation or obstacle
rule: Remarks about the impossibility/limitedness of a proposed action are 0 NEUTRAL if part of a joint search for a solution, without negative emotion or conflict.
example_ru: «— Не у всех нас есть хоботы, — заметил волчонок Зо.»

title: Joint action for the sake of helping
rule: Collective actions united by a shared goal of helping/supporting are +1 POSITIVE (cooperation, unity, mutual aid).
example_ru: «И все зверята ... отправились к Большой реке.»

title: End of misfortune and onset of well-being
rule: Fragments describing the resolution of a crisis, the return of life-sustaining conditions, or the end of misfortune are +1 POSITIVE.
example_ru: «Наконец ... на высохшую землю пролился долгожданный дождь.»

title: Weakly expressed negative emotion without dramatization → neutral
rule: Weak negative states (boredom, tiredness) without dramatization, suffering, conflict, or intensifying markers are 0 NEUTRAL if the state is not dominant and the next sentence neutralizes the accent; with suffering/complaint/conflict → -1 NEGATIVE.
example_ru: The airplane grew bored and looked down: A → -1, B → 0

title: Confrontational utterance with subsequent easing of tension
rule: If a segment opens with an aggressive/confrontational utterance and the continuation only softens its perception without changing its character, the label remains -1 NEGATIVE.
example_ru: «— Ну, давайте, наябедничайте! — вдруг заверещал самосвал...»
